researchSource.title: Land in the Indian Territory — selected 1859 removal report and 1882 delegates’ petition
researchSource.publisher: United States Senate / Government Printing Office; GovInfo digital copy
researchSource.type: Primary historical collection / reprinted administrative report and delegates’ petition
researchSource.annotation: This federal collection preserves an official removal account beside an Indigenous delegates’ petition. Their different dates, authors and purposes matter: arrival and administrative handover are not proof of consent, and a petition records a stated claim rather than a legal determination.
researchSource.countReason: One selected primary collection counted conservatively once. Two dated records and their reprinting are not inflated into separate source counts.
researchSource.contentReviewScope: Actual 84-page public PDF: cover/front matter p. 1; complete Robert S. Neighbors report dated September 3, 1859, printed/PDF p. 26; complete delegates’ petition dated April 1, 1882, p. 28, ending at its date/attestation before a separate Cheyenne–Arapaho text. Nearby estimates and later official arguments were encountered for context, not adopted as findings.
researchSource.citation: United States Senate. Land in the Indian Territory. Senate Executive Document 13, 48th Congress, 1st session, ordered printed December 19, 1883. Selected report of Robert S. Neighbors, September 3, 1859, p. 26; petition of delegates, April 1, 1882, p. 28.
researchSource.dateBasis: Printed cover identifies Congress/session and December 1883 transmission/printing. Reproduced records retain their own 1859 and 1882 dates.
researchSource.perspective: A federal compilation containing distinct voices: an agent’s account of his work and a petition signed/attested on behalf of named affiliated peoples. The surrounding collection includes officials contesting claims; its publication is not an endorsement of every assertion.
researchSource.accessStatus: Public English scanned PDF with extractable OCR; normal direct download succeeded
researchSource.accessNotes: Web tool rejected the 57,166,188-byte file as too large; normal HTTP 200 retrieval succeeded. No manuscript comparison or independent verification of the agent’s satisfaction/property claims. The letter does not independently identify every people in the Tribe’s later removal narrative. Petition boundaries, historic labels and claims are not converted into present territories, identities or legal rights.
researchSource.rightsNotes: Link and brief paraphrase only; no map, manuscript image, detailed property schedule or sensitive-place information reproduced.
